subject: Performance SLO (p95/p99) - hosted vs current provider - Post-call recap
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO (p95/p99) - hosted vs current provider - Post-call recap

Alex — thanks for the time earlier. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Key targets discussed:
- End-to-end p95 target: ~250 ms (UI->model token complete)
- End-to-end p99 target: <= 600 ms
- Target throughput: peak 200 req/s, sustained 120-150 req/s
- Concurrency target: ~40 concurrent requests (burst to 60)
- Streaming: yes — FinLytics needs partial streaming for chat UI to preserve perceived latency

What we heard from you on the call:
- Current provider p95/p99 are higher than your target (you mentioned p95 ~480 ms, p99 ~1.2s)
- Typical request payload ~3-5 KB (mostly short prompts + metadata)
- Peak load is spiky around market open — short bursts to 250 req/s for ~5-10m

Action items / next steps (proposed):
1) You: share current provider aggregate numbers, sample payloads, and any tracing logs you can provide for a representative window (we can accept scrubbed traces).
2) We (Redwood): run a hosted API benchmark that mirrors your traffic profile (payload size distribution, concurrency, streaming vs non-streaming) and report p95/p99, tail behavior, and resource/cost estimates.
3) Schedule a 2-hour benchmarking window next week (you confirm availability).
4) Exchange test plan & NDA if required — we'll provide a short test agreement and the benchmark instructions spreadsheet.

Attached: redwood_perf_summary.pdf — short note on Redwood hosted perf baseline and what our benchmark report will include.

If anything above is off, flag it and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll coordinate the test plan and propose available windows.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

---
Redwood Inference — Make LLM inference predictable and economical for production applications

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finlytics.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO (p95/p99) - hosted vs current provider - Post-call recap

Thanks Laura — that recap looks right. A few clarifications from our side and one request: 

Current provider numbers (last 30 days, production):
- p95: ~480 ms end-to-end (app front-end -> provider -> app)
- p99: ~1,200 ms
- Sustained throughput: ~150 req/s; short peaks to 250 req/s (5-12m windows)
- Concurrency during peaks: ~55 concurrent active sessions
- Typical payload: 3.8 KB median, 6 KB 95th percentile
- Streaming: yes — partial responses are used by our front-end for token-by-token display

We can share an aggregated CSV of request sizes and timestamps (attached: finlytics_current_perf.csv) and a small set of sanitized traces; please let us know the preferred format.

Request for Redwood: can you run an apples-to-apples hosted API benchmark that matches our payload distribution and concurrency (including streaming checks) and report the observed p95/p99 and any fallback behavior? We also need a clear statement on how Redwood's hosted offering handles overloads (queueing/batching/fallback to cheaper models) and whether streaming is supported end-to-end with similar tail latency.

Availability for a benchmark window: Tue 24 Mar 10:00-12:00 PT or Wed 25 Mar 13:00-15:00 PT. Prefer the earlier window if possible.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Turner
Head of Platform Engineering | FinLytics
alex.turner@finlytics.com
+1 (617) 555-0123

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO (p95/p99) - hosted vs current provider - Post-call recap

Alex — great, thanks for the numbers and the available windows. We can run the hosted benchmark for the Tue 24 Mar 10:00-12:00 PT window. Plan below: 

Planned benchmark scope:
- Synthetic traffic replay matching your payload size distribution (we'll use the attached finlytics_latency_test_plan.xlsx for the exact mix)
- Test cases: streaming vs non-streaming, varying concurrency (20/40/60), and short peak bursts to 250 req/s
- Metrics: end-to-end p50/p95/p99, CPU/GPU utilization, throughput, error rates, and latency distribution plots
- Deliverable: post-test report with raw logs, summarized charts, recommended config (batching, model variant, quantization) and estimated unit cost for production traffic levels

What we need from you by Mon EOD:
- A small sample set of production payloads (scrubbed) and the aggregated CSV you attached (we have it)
- Confirm whether you require us to sign an additional NDA/test agreement prior to running tests (link shared in related links)
- Any blackouts or maintenance windows on your side during Tue 24 Mar 10:00-12:00 PT

I’ll loop in our SRE and bench team (cc'd) — Marissa will own running the tests and will follow up with details and the test-run checklist.

Thanks,
Laura

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO (p95/p99) - hosted vs current provider - Post-call recap

Got it — I’ll own the benchmark run next Tue. Plan to:
- Validate payload replay tooling with the FinLytics CSV tonight
- Run a short smoke test Mon evening to sanity-check streaming paths
- Execute full matrix Tue 10:00-12:00 PT (20/40/60 concurrency, streaming vs non-streaming, bursts)
- Produce draft report by Wed 25 Mar EOD and share with Laura + Alex

I’ll also bring in an SRE (Vivek) for monitoring and to capture GPU utilization traces. Will update the test spreadsheet with the exact request mix and attach the run checklist.

 Marissa
